The diagram shown above is the slope field for which of the following differential equations?
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040443/assets/f3b0dad3f1cb4b2216e3fce7f1fefa8beac15a6e16ab09ab3a4c47a2472e2f9a.png)

 

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slope field is zero along the lines $y=-3$ and $y=0.$ Therefore, the right-hand side of the differential equation should evaluate to zero on these lines.

Of the given equations, the only two that satisfy this condition are

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{4}+3{y}^{3}={y}^{3}(y+3)
$$

 
and

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{3}+3{y}^{2}={y}^{2}(y+3).
$$

- Second, the lines $y=-3$ and $y=0$ divide the plane into $3$ regions. The sign of the slopes in each of the $3$ regions are easily deduced by considering the behavior of the solution curves in these regions. This information is summarized in the following table:

| Region | $y<-3$ | $-3<y<0$ | $y>0$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slope | $↗$ | $↘$ | $↗$ |
| Sign | $+$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Of the two remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{4}+3{y}^{3}={y}^{3}(y+3).
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}={y}^{4}+3{y}^{3}.$
